description:
## Goal

Define one World-owned, immutable, typed, path-aware input-flow relation for activation keying. The same extracted relation must support the current local-dispatch, forwarded-dispatch, and returned dimensions, and expose the typed callable-use sinks that `fz-kdt.165` will consume later. No dimension may rediscover a different approximation of how an input or call result moves.

## Current defect

The current `forwarded_inputs`, `input_positions`, and `returned_values` scans describe different incomplete graphs:

1. a `LoweredTail::DirectCall` result delivered through its destination is not correlated with the exact callsite and later use, so a discarded result can create false return dependence;
2. reconstructed arguments are not related to the input paths from which their fields came;
3. projected arguments, including protocol-callback forwarding, are not related;
4. expression map/field projection, map reconstruction, dynamic keys, and update overwrite semantics are not one exact typed path algebra;
5. a source-only returned mask loses which callee result path reached which caller result path.

These omissions already mint unbought activation keys or miss required distinctions. They would also make the later callable-identity dimension inherit another approximation.

## Correct model

Publish one immutable per-function input-flow fact derived once from `LoweredBody` plus `EntryDispatch`, or from `ProtocolDispatch` for a callback. Extern bodies retain their derived arity-sized local mask. Provider boundaries publish no path edges and an arity-sized all-`Ignore` local mask, so every consumer sees the same complete input coordinate space. Provider classification is one dependency-recording World query: every retained caller supplies its read sink, and the query records `ModuleDefined`, `FunctionDefined`, and `ModuleInterface` only when those mutable facts actually decide the answer. Blocked and concluding paths retain the same evidence, so interface arrival/replacement or a local module/function definition invalidates exactly the classifications it changes. Equal reproduction preserves the retained fact allocation and generation and wakes nobody.

The durable relation contains only typed semantic endpoints:

- origins are a function input path or one exact `CallSiteId` result path;
- sinks are a function-return path, a protocol input path, or a typed callable-use path;
- each direct callsite owns exactly one callee and one binding set per semantic input; a binding maps an origin to a destination path, an empty binding set represents a constant/local-only input, and an empty input sequence represents a zero-argument call;
- each mapping names its typed pullback: structural transport composes source and destination paths, while whole-origin dependency makes any non-bottom demand below the destination demand the complete named origin path;
- projection extends the source path and reconstruction extends the destination path;
- composition uses prefix/intersection semantics and returns residual paths, not a Boolean or path-length comparison;
- call results remain correlated by `CallSiteId`, so two calls to one callee never cross-connect;
- relation identity is normalized endpoint/path content with set semantics, not the syntactic route that produced it.

Paths use typed structural selectors. Tuple, list, bitstring, map, and struct paths are represented without display strings, canonical text, source spelling, raw interner order, `ValueId`, or `ControlEntryId` authority. Map and struct fields use exact typed keys. Every literal runtime map-key denotation is retained: atoms (including boolean/nil atom forms), integers, bit-exact floats, and binary bytes. Raw and UTF-8 literal carriers that denote the same runtime binary normalize to one key. Dynamic map access/update has an explicit conservative any-key/root dependency: projecting or transporting the selected result never invents the same projection below the key origin. Selector identity is normalized (`DynamicExcept([])` is `Dynamic`), intersections retain their exact residual exclusions, known-key updates exclude overwritten base fields, and the last duplicate write owns its key.

Delivery provenance follows the actual control-flow graph. `AssertSame` equivalence flows to dominated successor entries; a merge retains only equivalences true on every incoming path, while each delivered local value is resolved with its producer path's equivalence before the paths join. A direct-call return reaches only its own return or delivered resume; a discarded delivery creates no returned edge. Result paths remain explicit so projecting one returned field does not pull unrelated fields.

The relation is extraction, not a cross-function scheduler. Current `InputDemand` derivation consumes it through one temporary callsite-scoped query solver for its three dimensions. Forwarded dispatch follows every reachable call argument; returned demand additionally composes the exact callee input-to-result relation with that callsite’s exact result-to-caller-sink relation. Those are different edge selections over one relation, not one filtered approximation. Returned demand is a may-dependency: a local base-return flow remains authoritative even when another recursive edge supplies that input locally. Empty bindings contribute no pullback at that exact call edge; they may not erase an independent flow or another callsite. No function-wide supplied-position subtraction is sound without retained proof that every external seed is equal.

Local extraction and acyclic composition are exact. The current finite-tree `DispatchDemand` cannot represent every infinite recursive path language, so only queries, ports, and answers owned by recursive strongly connected components are normalized below a deterministic structural frontier `K`. `K` is computed once from the SCC condensation DAG, and the normalizer is extensive, monotone, and idempotent (`q <= N_K(q)`): it can add demand but cannot lose a needed dependency. Callsite routing remains exact, constructors above the frontier remain distinct, and acyclic paths are never normalized. This is an explicitly temporary sound over-approximation, not a claim that `K` preserves every finite recursive precision result.

## TDD

- A direct tail call has one owned callsite record with its unique callee and exact per-input mappings plus its call-result-to-return path; zero-argument, all-constant, and mixed constant/projected calls remain discoverable without duplicate metadata.
- An `InputFlow`-only request for an ordinary function with no `LoweredBody` waits on and pulls that exact producer; only a proven provider boundary publishes the edge-empty arity-sized answer. Interface-first and source/root-plus-`InputFlow`/`StaticCallees`-demand-first schedules converge to the same provider relation and native edge.
- An `InputFlow` derivation that has observed `ModuleDefined` or `LoweredBody` and must next wait for `ProtocolDispatch` or `EntryDispatch` retains every earlier observation while blocked; relevant replacement during that wait invalidates the standing prior relation.
- Two callsites to one callee remain isolated; a returned result propagates demand and a delivered/discarded result does not.
- A callee result field reconstructed into a different caller result field composes across coordinate systems; sibling fields do not cross-connect.
- A delivered result projected or reconstructed in its resume retains the exact result and destination paths; unrelated fields do not appear.
- Tuple and list projection/reconstruction compose exact source and destination paths, including `Head`, `Tail`, `Tail/Head`, and negative sibling/tail controls.
- Map and struct relation paths distinguish every literal runtime key by one normalized typed denotation (atoms including boolean/nil forms, integers, bit-exact floats, and binary bytes across raw/UTF-8 carriers); empty exclusions normalize away; dynamic selectors and remainders retain exact residual exclusions when they intersect; a projection below a dynamic lookup result pulls the entire key origin locally and across a call; known-key update overwrite and duplicate-last-write semantics are exact; `MapIndex`, `FieldAccess`, and `RequireMapValue` agree.
- Reachable `AssertSame` equivalence survives branches and delivery to dominated uses, while a one-arm assertion does not leak through a merge or conflate mutually exclusive arms.
- Protocol forwarding maps callback paths to implementation paths, ignores absent callbacks, and is invariant to arm order and duplicates.
- Duplicate edges and source/job order reproduce the equal retained fact without replacing its allocation, advancing generation, or waking readers.
- Interface replacement, module definition, and function definition each wake exactly the retained `InputFlow`, root/target `StaticCallees`, call-graph, and semantic direct-call decisions that observed provider classification; global, source-owned, and runtime functions add no irrelevant classification read.
- Local extraction remains finite for self and mutual recursion.
- A local base return remains demanded even when one or more self-calls pass a constant or locally rebuilt value at that input; one callsite cannot erase a dependency carried by another.
- Pullback through a recursive edge remains path-exact: reconstructing only one carried child retains that child and not its siblings. Identity and permutation controls remain exact.
- Recursive demand normalization preserves bottom, is extensive, monotone, and idempotent; genuine self and mutual structural growth terminate without widening unrelated fields, while acyclic repeated-call composition remains exact.
- Production-boundary fixtures prove delivered-result, reconstructed-argument, projected protocol-callback, direct-forwarding, and unrelated-field behavior across interpreter, JIT, and build doors with exact activation counts and no warnings.

## Required deletion

- Delete `ForwardEdge`, `forwarded_inputs`, `input_positions`, `extend_positions`, `returned_values`, and their duplicate construction/projection scans.
- Replace private `DemandPathStep` with the shared typed path algebra used by dispatch subjects and flow extraction.
- Replace bespoke protocol forwarding extraction with the same relation.
- Delete the unsound function-wide recursion-supply calculation. Let the temporary callsite-scoped query solver consume the relation without rescanning `LoweredBody`; `fz-kdt.213` owns deletion of that private cone/query scheduling.
- Delete the dependency-free provider-boundary Boolean/parallel observation API; no retained derivation may classify a provider without supplying the read set that owns its conclusion.
- Leave no compatibility relation, route-history identity, string/raw-ID ordering, probe, generated fixture sidecar, migration test, or temporary telemetry.

## Acceptance

- The current three `InputDemand` dimensions consume one typed path relation; the relation exposes callable-use sinks for the later fourth dimension without changing callable-identity behavior in this ticket.
- Every supported semantic mapping has one normalized identity and one constructor path.
- No dimension-specific forwarding/provenance scan or second relation authority remains.
- Relation equality and iteration are deterministic across entry, arm, source, and job order; equal reproduction retains allocation and does no downstream work.
- Provider-boundary classification has one dependency-recording authority shared by `InputFlow`, `StaticCallees`, call-graph keying, and semantic direct-call selection. Every mutable deciding fact is retained through waits and conclusions; no irrelevant read is added when immutable/global/source/runtime state already decides the answer.
- Exact relation-set tests cover every typed selector and composition law. Acyclic composition remains exact. Recursive SCC demand may conservatively over-key only below its deterministic structural frontier; it never under-keys, lets one recursive edge erase an independent may-flow, crosses callsites, normalizes an acyclic path, or widens an unrelated constructor above the frontier.
- Focused keying/protocol/reconstruction/map/list/alias tests, all three target doors, full serial library and fixture matrix, cross-process determinism, formatting, documentation checks, `cargo check`, and strict clippy pass.
- A fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review accepts the final diff before its one commit and close.

## Boundaries and ordering

`fz-kdt.200` follows this ticket, replaces `DispatchDemand::Whole` with the final finite-height question axes over this relation, and deletes the temporary SCC structural budget, `N_K` normalizer, and policy-specific over-approximation tests. `fz-kdt.213` then owns reactive cross-function convergence and removal of the private cone/query scheduling. `fz-kdt.165` owns the fourth `InputDemand` component and deletion of `BodyKeying::consumes_callable_identity`. `fz-tfn.42` owns runtime return-payload type/demand. This ticket does not absorb those changes.\u0000\u0000

comments.text: fz-kdt.199 landed (dd07432db) and names this ticket in return_flow_mask's doc and in type-specialization.md with all three holes. The returned axis is solved over the same forwarding cone as fz-kdt.183's dispatch axis, so it inherits that cone's edge set exactly: a DirectCall dest is ignored (deliver2.fz keys 7 -> 9 for nothing), a RECONSTRUCTED argument is not an edge (hops.fz: outer/2 stays collapsed while inner/2 and mid/2 split, so two keys both publish the join -- 2 executables for 0 precision), and a PROJECTED argument is not an edge (proto_cb.fz, the protocol-callback case). One edge-set improvement serves three axes: 183's dispatch, 199's returned, and fz-kdt.165's planned identity axis on the same walk.

title: Define one exact typed path-aware InputDemand flow relation
